review_notes: Source-first scope: the introduction identifies discretionary accruals, real-activities manipulation, and AAER incidence as the three main earnings-management outcomes. Retained the full-sample ABS_DA model in Table 3, all four distinct outcomes in the paper’s main real-activities family in Table 4, and both AAER outcomes in Table 5 Panel B. Excluded Table 3 directional accrual columns, later KLD-category and alternative CSR measures, and subsequent subgroup/robustness analyses.

The paper does not name the underlying estimator for its multiple-regression models or its construction regressions. Table 5 calls Equation (3) a logistic regression, while the printed equation presents Pr(AAER=1) as a linear expression plus an error and supplies no link; this source inconsistency remains unresolved. The two-digit SIC-year advertising-intensity aggregation and total-accrual component calculation are not reported. The annual industry classification for the discretionary-accrual construction and all supporting-fit cell Ns are not reported.
results_review_notes: Table 2 Panel A reports full-sample n, mean, median, standard deviation, 25th percentile, and 75th percentile for each retained variable shown there. DA is linked as a raw version of ABS_DA; Age of firm (in years) is linked as a raw version of FIRM_AGE; AB_CFO, AB_PROD, and AB_EXP are linked as components of COMBINED_RAM.

Table 2 Panel B subgroup means and medians are preserved for CSR and non-CSR samples; table difference-test p-values are not variable descriptives. Panel C quartile frequencies and Panel A Table 5 AAER cross-tab frequencies are retained as reported counts/shares. Table 2 Panel D correlations and chi-square/LR hypothesis tests are excluded from variable descriptives.

Selected fit statistics (industry-dummy status, adjusted/max-rescaled R², likelihood ratio, and n) are preserved in each result_set.review_notes because the frozen enrichment schema has no dedicated fit-statistic property.
